At the core of the X-men/Mutant stories within Marvel comics there are a series of conflicts. These largely revolve around dealing with the self and the community when one does not necessarily fit the community's defined vision of itself. The conflict draws many parallels with the real world but is most focused on the race relations in the United States and are rooted in Malcom X as represented by Magneto and Martin Luther King Jr. as presented by Professor X. Extremism and violence versus peaceful protest and political persuasion. Secondarily it uses imagery and allusion to the Third Reich and Holocaust.

Within the Mutant stories there is the root of all the conflict, the difference in power between the Superiour and the Sapien species, and from there different levels of communal attachment and disassociation arise.

There are the sentient beings within the dimension, and they defend their version of reality when it is threatened, but it is not united unless threatened. Every organism and organisation is willing to stand together when they are all threatened, but only then.

There are the galactic empires and alliances, which hold together and defend themselves from one another's interference and major threats, but they are still divided by worlds. No empire will come to the aid of another against the likes of Galactus or Thanos.

There is the population of Earth, and when it is threatened, everyone comes to it's defense, but each nation still considers it's own interests first.

There are the races of Superiour and Sapien, which when directly threatened by the other unite against the common threat, but they are not united.

There are the unifiers and peacemakers who wish to include both races together, like Xavier and Hank McCoy, and many others. But they are divided into teams, and groups, and national lines.

There are those who wish for Superior to rise above Sapien, either as the new leaders, or as the replacement species... Magneto, Apocalypse, Sinister.

There are those who wish to eliminate this new threat to the Sapien species and consequently seek it's destruction to preserve humanity as it is, Bolivar Trask, Graydon Creed.

There are the ones who work within the system, and those who work without among the Superiours... The X-men, X-force, whathaveyou, and then the Morlocks, the Brotherhood, various cults.

There are also the legally recognized heroes and villains vs the vigilantes, S.H.I.E.L.D. and Weapon X being directed and funded by government agencies. Whereas the Punisher, X-men and the Fantastic Four are self funded and will on occasion clash with authorities.

Then still there are racial boundaries within the Sapien communities and nations, same bullshit that is in the real world, but toned down significantly, because many who would blame racial traits have the larger target of mutants in this reality.

Everyone gets divided up eventually, all conflicts within the series rise from a lack of unity for various reasons.

They are used as parallels for racism, religious differences, the Red Menace of Communism, the threat of Authoritarianism, homosexuality, transexuality, polygamy, humanism, transhumanism, nature vs technology, genetic engineering and eugenics... any and all topics can find parallels to work with.

James Howlett/Logan/Wolverine is a mutant who is very old, so he does not fit in entirely with the current generation - despite being Canadian he was raised in a period when Canada was very British, the Klondike Gold Rush was still happening. He serves as a Man Out of Time like Captain America, but he has lived through it all rather than jumping through time. He works for an American vigilante organization, the X-men, where he serves under Xavier, but does not entirely agree with the placations and supplicative manner by which Charles operates. He has been a CIA operative, a sheriff, a private investigator... Working both inside and outside the law. He has mutant powers but was also augmented by a clandestine government body. He has studied the history and martial arts of multiple nations and knows many languages, he is called a ronin by observers. He is often used for interesting stories because he walks so many lines.

Unfortunately this great number of lines he walks is what makes him overused. Writers have attempted to explore every aspect of these intersecting loyalties and interests. He has fought for and against almost every major team at least once.
